questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.category: Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids :: Organic Reaction Pathway (Type 1)
questions.question: An equimolar mixture of benzaldehyde and formaldehyde is treated with concentrated $(50\%)$ aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ (Crossed Cannizzaro condition) in [Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids]. What are the major products isolated after acidification?
questions.solution: Formaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogens and is far more electrophilic than benzaldehyde. Nucleophilic addition of $\text{OH}^-$ occurs rapidly on formaldehyde, forming an intermediate that transfers hydride $(\text{H}^-)$ to benzaldehyde. Formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate, and benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol.
questions.explanation: Deduce using established organic reaction mechanisms in Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.category: Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids :: Stoichiometric Reaction Calculation
questions.question: In [Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids], how many moles of $\text{NaOH}$ are consumed in the complete haloform reaction of one mole of acetone $(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3)$ with iodine to form iodoform and sodium acetate?
questions.solution: The balanced equation is: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \longrightarrow \text{CHI}_3\downarrow + \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Exactly $4$ moles of $\text{NaOH}$ are consumed.
questions.explanation: Solve using reaction stoichiometry in Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids.
